With that preamble, one of the first issues addressed in finance is the agency problem. Before the time value of money, the cost of capital, and the various sources of financing, the risk posed by the diverging interests between shareholders and management is defined. Stated simply, decision makers in any enterprise are the agents of the shareholder, but the interest and incentives of these agents can and will differ from those of the shareholder. Hence, the agency problem: when a manager makes decisions in the interest of him or herself not the shareholders. 

For the shareholder, the hope of AI is that the AI agent can be trained to act in their interest alone and have no outside interest or incintive. Saving money would be an added bonus. Executives are expensive and unreliable. They imagine an agent that will antipate and react -- 

The real challenge with this desire is that the interests of shareholders differ. If one considers investing in corporate America - aka the stock market - he or she would find a variety of investors - the shareholders in the company. New companies have founders heavily invested. Amazon has Jeff Bezos. Meta has Mark Zuckerberg. Microsoft still has Bill Gates. Older companies have the children and grandchildren of founders. Ford has the Ford family. Walmart has the Waltons. Other individual investors like owning a share of corporate America - either for the regular dividends that come each quarter or the promise of gain on the capital their share represents. Add in institutions like mutual funds and pensions who own stock on behalf of others and you have a diverse set of shareholders with different timelines and objectives.

A founder's objective might be creating their vision of the future. Henry Ford envisioned a future with a car specifically a Ford in every garage in America. Sam Walton imagined a Walmart in every community in America. Jeff Bezos is imagining a world where autonoumous drones drop off items on a customer's door step and a world of entertainment is available at the click of a button. 

For a founders decendents, their objective might be preserving the founder's legacy by maintaining their vision or collecting dividends on what that vision earns now.

For some individual investors, it might be a quick profit so they can spend their remaining days in luxary. For other investors, it might be preserving the capital they have accumulated through out their career.

These interests inivitably clash - think of the premise of the film The Social Network.
